r0058: 33.  The Court observes that on 9 October 1987 the applicant obtained an order for possession, the enforcement of which had been set by the magistrate (*juge d’instance*) for 9 October 1988 (see paragraph 13 above). Notwithstanding the fact that, from 1991, the tenant had been in arrears with the rent – of which the applicant had informed the authorities (see paragraph 17 above) – and that, accordingly, the statutory conditions for enforcing the eviction during the period in which that procedure was suspended had been satisfied in the present case, the applicant did not obtain police assistance until 2 July 1993 (see paragraph 19 above). The applicant had not only had to bring proceedings to resolve the problem of the partly unpaid rent (see paragraph 17 above), but had also had to pay himself the tenant’s share of the service charges, following a payment order obtained by the managing agent of the building (see paragraph 20 above).
r0059: 34.  In those circumstances, the Court considers that the restriction on the applicant’s use of his apartment, resulting in particular from the improper application by the competent authorities of the exceptions to the suspension of the provision of police assistance, imposed an individual and excessive burden on him and accordingly upset the balance to be struck between the protection of the individual’s right to the peaceful enjoyment of his possessions and the requirements of the general interest (see, mutatis mutandis, Scollo v. Italy, judgment of 28 September 1995, Series A no. 315-C, § 39).
r0060: There has accordingly been a violation of Article 1 of Protocol No. 1.
r0061: II.  ALLEGED VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 6 § 1 OF THE CONVENTION
r0062: 35.  The applicant also alleged a breach of Article 6 § 1 of the Convention, the relevant part of which provides:
r0063: “In the determination of his civil rights and obligations ..., everyone is entitled to a ... hearing within a reasonable time by [a] ... tribunal ...”
r0065: 36.  The Government raised the same objections to the admissibility of this complaint – the inapplicability of Article 6 to proceedings for the eviction of a tenant and failure to exhaust domestic remedies – as they had already raised and which had been dismissed by the Commission in its decision on the admissibility of the present application.
r0066: The Court considers that they must be dismissed for the same reasons.
